taxonomic_note: Accepted species but non-native in Texas.
look_here_first: KLEINGRASS: INTRODUCED African perennial forage TUFT, often tall and knotty at its center, with fine open branching panicles. Look for firm basal perennial growth, then confirm Panicum spikelet anatomy and collar. Existing two real photos show general habit, NOT precise ligule, glume length or crown cross section; never treat the naturalized Texas presence as county-native evidence.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Panicum coloratum but gives its native range as Egypt to southern Africa and explicitly lists Texas as introduced. Texas A&M Rangelands describes Kleingrass as an introduced warm-season perennial brought from Africa. Texas specimen records, including Hays County, are introduced/naturalized occurrences and therefore do not count toward the project native threshold.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

crew_field_check: KLEINGRASS: INTRODUCED African perennial forage TUFT, often tall and knotty at its center, with fine open branching panicles. Look for firm basal perennial growth, then confirm Panicum spikelet anatomy and collar. Existing two real photos show general habit, NOT precise ligule, glume length or crown cross section; never treat the naturalized Texas presence as county-native evidence.

Unlike short native blue-gray P. hallii, Kleingrass often makes substantial robust cultivated or naturalized bunches; unlike witchgrass it is perennial without coarse hairy annual stems; unlike rhizomatous switchgrass don't infer a switchgrass white collar patch from a small panoramic photo.
Examine the same plant's crown, collar and mature spikelet with a millimeter scale before assigning difficult specimens.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Panicum virgatum: Switchgrass is native, rhizomatous, and has a characteristic hairy collar; Kleingrass is introduced and typically has a firm knotty base. Panicum hallii: Hall's panicum is smaller, glaucous and native, with a more compact stiff-branched panicle.

field_id_lesson.look_here_first: Kleingrass is an introduced perennial forage bunchgrass with a firm often knotty crown and an open, fine-branched panicle. Confirm at collar and mature spikelet; do not confuse with native switchgrass.

measured_checks.growth: Perennial tuft, often knotty at base.
measured_checks.ligule: Hair-fringed ligule; macro and scale needed.
measured_checks.panicle: Open, diffuse; document full length and branch attachment.
measured_checks.spikelets: Small, generally a few millimeters; measure before final identification.
measured_checks.glumes: Lower glume notably shorter than spikelet in published keys; verify proportion on mature spikelet.
measured_checks.lemma: Inspect fertile upper floret and lower sterile lemma; close macro needed.
measured_checks.awns: No awn inference from distant panicle images.

lookalikes: Panicum hallii: usually shorter glaucous tuft and smaller ascending panicle.
Panicum virgatum: native switchgrass, often rhizomatous with different crown and spikelet characters.
Panicum capillare: annual with conspicuously hairy sheaths and very diffuse panicle.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: KLEINGRASS: trace an open 4–30 cm panicle to a rooted, knotty perennial TUFT, then measure solitary, awnless 2–3.2 mm spikelets. The LOWER glume is only about one-quarter to one-third of spikelet length; don't confuse this introduced forage grass with native Hall's panicgrass or switchgrass by head shape alone.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form: Introduced African tufted perennial, sometimes shortly rhizomatous; stems often 15–100 cm but taller in some regional treatments. Confirm attached perennial crown rather than inferring it from a cut flowering culm.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.ligule_collar: True ligule is a ciliate-edged membrane; regional treatments give approximately 0.5–2.5 mm (VicFlora), while Flora of China gives 0.5–1 mm. Blades generally 2–12 mm wide, with sheath hairiness variable. Photograph the true blade–sheath junction separately from any neighboring sheath hairs.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.panicle_spikelets: Open to partly contracted branched panicle usually 4–30 cm; spikelets solitary, pedicelled, ovate-elliptic, approximately 2–3.2 mm, dorsally compressed, awnless. Panicle silhouette alone is not species-diagnostic.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.glumes: Lower glume cufflike, approximately 0.7–1 mm, generally 1-veined (occasionally up to 3), only one-quarter to one-third of mature spikelet length. Upper glume approximately spikelet-length, 7–9-veined.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.lemmas_palea_awns: Lower floret is staminate in cited treatments, with membranous lower lemma approximately spikelet-length and a developed palea. Upper fertile lemma approximately 1.5–2.5 mm, firm, smooth, shiny and inrolled around palea. No true awns; do not label slender panicle pedicels as awns.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.central_texas_lookalikes: P. hallii is typically smaller, stiff, blue-glaucous and basal-leaved; P. capillare is a hairy annual with diffuse tumbleweed-like head; P. virgatum is usually rhizomatous with a characteristic triangular white-hair patch on upper blade base. Verify roots, ligule and spikelet glumes rather than using height or forage habitat alone.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Kleingrass — verify forage bunch then obtain real panicle and ligule anatomy
steps: FIRST see the USDA field reference: a relatively robust tuft of upright flowering stems; photograph the actual plant base and stem attachment before inferring a rooted crown.

SECOND compare the independently sourced CC0 tuft photo, which has green-and-dry basal blades and thin upright stems. It does not show the actual collar, measured spikelets or diagnostic seedhead close-up.
THIRD examine the separately identified Panicum hallii look-alike: its smaller rocky-site basal clump and curling dried leaf blades can be suggestive but size and dry leaf curl are not decisive.
FOURTH photograph a genuine mature P. coloratum panicle on the same documented plant from full-branch and 10–20× views; retain spikelets on the stalk and measure their length with a 1-mm ruler.

FIFTH split the fresh same-plant blade–sheath junction to show actual membranous/ciliate ligule, collar, sheath hairs and nodes; dissect and photograph measured glumes, sterile floret and shiny fertile lemma before asserting species.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: The archived photographs prove broad field habit only. Certify kleingrass from a matched, source-determined flowering panicle with measured spikelets and actual collar anatomy—not from size or a forage planting alone.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Only two source-labelled CC0/public-domain local species photographs. Neither provides a verified flowering close-up, ligule or mature spikelet anatomy; no speculative anatomical arrows have been added.
